provider.name: Shopify
provider.description: Shopify is an e-commerce platform that allows developers to build applications using the GraphQL Admin API and OAuth authentication.

authMethod.text: OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code Grant or Token Exchange)
authMethod.quote: Shopify is an e-commerce platform. This toolkit is GraphQL-first for new Admin API automations while retaining legacy REST compatibility actions for older workflows and numeric-ID interoperability

difficulty.rationale: Requires managing client credentials, strict scoping, test store setup, billing integration, and public review for app store distribution.

handsOnEffort.basis: Assumes creating a Partner account, setting up an app in the Dev Dashboard, configuring scopes, and wiring custom credentials into Composio.

summary.text: Public apps intended for the Shopify App Store must pass an external app review before distribution.
summary.quote: Before you submit your app to Shopify, you should do some final tests, validations, and administrative tasks to ensure that it's ready for review, and ready for merchants to use the app in production.

triggers.text: Requesting access to protected customer data requires additional approval in the Partner Dashboard.

steps.actorReason: Creating accounts requires human identity and legal agreement.
steps.text: Register for a Shopify Partner account to begin building apps.

steps.title: Create an App in the Dev Dashboard
steps.action: Navigate to Apps, click create app, and configure your app name and settings.
steps.actorReason: Developer console actions require a logged-in human user.

steps.quote: 1. Log in to your Dev Dashboard. 2. Click Apps. 3. Click the name of your app to navigate to the App overview page.

steps.title: Configure Redirect URIs and Scopes
steps.action: Set your app URL and allowed redirection URLs in the app configuration.
steps.actorReason: An agent can draft redirect URLs and scope lists, but a human must save them in the console.

steps.title: Create a Custom Auth Config in Composio
steps.action: Create an OAuth2 auth config in Composio and paste your Shopify Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.actorReason: Entering sensitive credentials into Composio requires a human developer.
steps.text: Create the auth config in the Composio dashboard and enter the required credential fields.

steps.title: Add Composio Redirect URI to Shopify App
steps.action: Add the OAuth redirect URI provided by Composio into your allowed redirection URLs in the Shopify Dev Dashboard.
steps.actorReason: An agent can supply the exact URI string, but a human must paste it into the console.
steps.text: For OAuth toolkits, the dashboard shows the redirect URI to add in the provider's developer portal.

steps.action: Install your app on a development store to test authentication and API calls.
steps.actorReason: Installing apps on a dev store requires manual human execution.

risks.text: Public apps must use expiring offline access tokens; non-expiring tokens will be blocked from API requests starting April 1, 2027.
risks.quote: Public apps that still use non-expiring offline access tokens are delisted and blocked from new installs on January 1, 2027. Their GraphQL Admin API and REST Admin API requests are rejected from April 1, 2027.

risks.text: Submitting incomplete apps or apps with broken billing or installation flows will result in rejection and require resubmission.
risks.quote: If you submit an app that is incomplete or has errors that prevent us from reviewing its features, then it won't be approved.

faq.question: How do I set up custom OAuth credentials for Shopify?
faq.answer: For a step-by-step guide on creating and configuring your own Shopify OAuth credentials with Composio, see [How to create OAuth credentials for Shopify](https://composio.dev/auth/shopify).

faq.question: Why am I seeing "App not found" when connecting Shopify?
faq.answer: The default Shopify OAuth app may be under review or expired. Use your own OAuth app or API authentication method until the default is restored.

faq.question: Shopify order update 403s can be caused by missing `read_all_orders` scope
faq.answer: Check the scopes on the Shopify connection. If order reads or updates require access beyond the default order scope set, reconnect with the needed order scopes such as `read_all_orders` before retrying.
